decisive_items: Cultures of lung fluid and blood were positive
Massive pleural effusion in the right lower lung lobe
Shows disappearance of the massive empyema after treatment
response.rationale: Cirrhosis with Child-Pugh C predisposes to spontaneous bacterial infection; positive pleural fluid cultures and imaging-confirmed empyema that resolved after treatment point to spontaneous bacterial empyema, more specific than generic empyema or sepsis.

rejected.why: Hepatohydraulic syndrome is not an infection and lacks positive culture support.
Peritonitis is abdominal, not pleural; no ascites or peritoneal signs.
Pleural empyema is less specific, missing the spontaneous bacterial context in cirrhosis.
Sepsis is a systemic response, not the localized pleural infection diagnosis.
Hepatopulmonary syndrome involves intrapulmonary shunting, not pleural infection or positive cultures.
